topics.title: Kinematics
topics.description: The description of motion — position, velocity, and acceleration without regard to cause.
objectives: Define position, displacement, velocity, and acceleration
Apply kinematic equations for constant acceleration

problem_templates.prompt_template: A car accelerates from rest at 3 m/s². Find its velocity and displacement after 8 seconds using the kinematic equations. Show which equation you choose and why.
A ball is launched at 45° with initial speed 20 m/s. Find (a) the maximum height, (b) the range, and (c) the time of flight. Use component-wise kinematic equations and g = 9.8 m/s².
Two trains leave the same station: Train A at 40 m/s, Train B departing 10 s later at 60 m/s in the same direction. At what time and position does Train B overtake Train A? Show the algebraic setup.

topics.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
topics.description: The three laws governing the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.
objectives: State and apply Newton's three laws
Apply Newton's laws to inclines and pulleys

problem_templates.prompt_template: A 5 kg block sits on a frictionless surface. Three horizontal forces act on it: 10 N east, 6 N west, 4 N west. Draw a free-body diagram, find the net force, and compute the acceleration.
Two masses m₁ = 3 kg and m₂ = 5 kg are connected by a string over a frictionless pulley (Atwood machine). Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string. Draw FBDs for each mass.

A block of mass 4 kg is on a 30° incline with μ_k = 0.2. It is pulled up the incline by a force F parallel to the surface. Find the minimum F to move it at constant velocity. Include friction in the FBD.

topics.title: Work and Energy
topics.description: Energy as the capacity to do work — kinetic, potential, and conservation of energy.
objectives: Define work as force times displacement

problem_templates.prompt_template: A 2 kg box is pushed 5 m along a frictionless floor by a 15 N horizontal force. Compute the work done, the final kinetic energy, and the final speed (starting from rest). Use the work-energy theorem.

A 0.5 kg ball is dropped from 10 m. Using conservation of energy (ignoring air resistance), find its speed just before hitting the ground. Then redo the calculation assuming 20% of energy is lost to air resistance.
A spring with k = 500 N/m is compressed 0.2 m and launches a 0.1 kg ball up a frictionless 30° ramp. How far along the ramp does the ball travel before stopping? Use energy methods throughout.

topics.title: Momentum and Impulse
topics.description: Momentum as mass times velocity; the impulse-momentum theorem and conservation.
objectives: Apply conservation of momentum to collisions

problem_templates.prompt_template: A 1500 kg car moving at 20 m/s collides with a stationary 1000 kg car. They stick together (perfectly inelastic). Find their common velocity after collision. What fraction of kinetic energy is lost?
A 0.05 kg bullet fired at 400 m/s embeds in a 2 kg block on a frictionless surface. Find the block's velocity. Then the block slides up a frictionless ramp — how high does it reach?
A 3 kg ball (v = 5 m/s east) has a perfectly elastic collision with a stationary 1 kg ball. Derive both final velocities using conservation of momentum AND kinetic energy simultaneously.

topics.title: Rotational Motion
topics.description: Extension of kinematics and Newton's laws to rotating bodies — torque, angular momentum.
objectives: Define angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration
Compute torque and moment of inertia

problem_templates.prompt_template: A wheel starts from rest and reaches 120 rpm in 5 seconds with constant angular acceleration. Find α, the number of revolutions completed, and the final angular velocity in rad/s.
A solid cylinder (mass 4 kg, radius 0.3 m) rolls without slipping down a 20° incline from height 2 m. Find its speed at the bottom using energy conservation with rotational KE. I = ½mr².

A figure skater pulls her arms in, reducing her moment of inertia from 4 kg·m² to 1.5 kg·m². If she starts at 1 rev/s, find her final angular velocity. Compute the ratio of final to initial kinetic energy and explain the source of the extra energy.

topics.title: Oscillations and Waves
topics.description: Simple harmonic motion and wave phenomena — springs, pendulums, and wave properties.
objectives: Define wave speed, frequency, and wavelength

problem_templates.prompt_template: A mass of 0.4 kg on a spring (k = 100 N/m) is released from x = 0.05 m. Write x(t) for the position, find the period T, and compute the maximum speed and acceleration.
A simple pendulum has period 2 s on Earth. Find its length. If taken to Mars where g = 3.72 m/s², what is its new period? What length would give T = 2 s on Mars?
Two waves on a string: y₁ = 3 sin(2πx − 6πt) and y₂ = 3 sin(2πx + 6πt). Find the superposition y = y₁ + y₂ using the sum-to-product identity. Identify nodes and antinodes.
